abstract: Impairment of the blood-brain barrier (BBB) is often observed in Alzheimer's disease patients, especially those who carry the APOE4 allele of apolipoprotein E. Brain pericytes are crucial for maintaining the BBB. Yet, the mechanisms linking APOE genetic variation to pericyte-mediated pathologies are not fully understood. Given the importance of pericyte-secreted factors in cerebrovascular homeostasis, we hypothesized that the protein and lipid compositions of pericyte-secreted apoE lipoproteins (LpEs) would differ depending on the APOE genotype. Using liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry, we investigated the lipid and protein components of LpEs secreted by human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived APOE-isogenic pericytes. Our results demonstrate that APOE2/E2, APOE3/E3, and APOE4/E4 pericytes secrete LpEs with distinct lipid and protein compositions. ApoE4 particles (LpE4) have high total lipid levels, LpE3 are enriched in ether-linked phospholipids, and LpE2 in ester-linked phosphatidylcholines and short-chain sphingomyelins. Extracellular matrix proteins are highly represented in LpE4, followed by LpE2. In particular, fibronectin is abundant in LpE4 and LpE2, but not in LpE3. While cellular lipid levels and lipid subclass compositions also differ between APOE-isogenic pericytes, they do not mirror the lipid profiles of secreted LpE. The most differentially abundant cellular lipid subclasses include triglycerides, sphingomyelins, glycosphingolipids (Hex3Cer, Hex2Cer, HexCer), and ceramides. In conclusion, the composition of pericyte-secreted LpEs varies by APOE genotype, suggesting distinct functions in brain homeostasis and neurodegenerative disease. Differences in cellular lipids further suggest APOE-mediated changes in lipid metabolism, highlighting the role of vascular cells in brain health and disease.
